questions.question: The 'Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan' (PM-AASHA) has________ components to rationalise the government agricultural produce price and policy for efficiency, savings by way of reduction of wastages and leakages in storage and make fiscal gains.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan' (PM-AASHA)** has **three **components to rationalise the government agricultural produce price and policy for efficiency, savings by way of reduction of wastages and leakages in storage and making fiscal gains.
 
• It is a scheme that guarantees a **Minimum support price (MSP)** to the farmers.
 
• The scheme is an effort of the government’s commitment to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their produce as announced in the **Union Budget for 2018. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The scheme comprises three sub-schemes:**

 
 
• Price Support Scheme (PSS)

 
 
• ​Under this, physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds, and Copra is to be done by Central Nodal Agencies in collaboration with state governments.
 
 
 
• Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS)
 
 
• ​This is based on the recommendations of NITI Aayog which suggested “Price Deficiency Payment” for implementation of MSP in crops where procurement is poor.
 
• Direct payment of the difference between the MSP and the selling price will be made to pre-registered farmers selling their produce in the notified market yard and thus it does not involve any physical procurement.
 
 
 
• The pilot of the Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPPS)
 
 
• Under this scheme, participation of the private sector in procurement operations will be piloted.
 
• States have the option to roll out the scheme on a pilot basis in selected districts/APMCs involving private stockists.
 
 
 
 

92

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) scheme launched by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2009**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA)** is a centrally funded scheme run by **India's Ministry of Human Resource Development **to improve secondary education in public schools across the country.
 
• It was first released in March of **2009**. The scheme's implementation began in 2009-2010 with the goal of creating circumstances for efficient growth, development, and equity for all.
 
• Multidimensional research, technical consulting, numerous implementations, and financial support are all part of the plan.
 
• **The main goals were to improve secondary education quality and to increase total enrollment from 52 percent in 2005–2006 to 75 percent in five years, from 2009 to 2014.**
 
• Its goal was to provide universal education to all children aged 15 to 16. The central ministry funds are channelled through state governments, which set up their own implementation organisations.

questions.question: What is the amount of annual health cover available to a family under the 'Ayushman Bharat' scheme of the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ ​5 Lakh__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ​Ayushman Bharat- Pradhan Mantri Jan ArogyaYojana (PMJAY) will provide a cover of up to Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year, for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
• This is the “world’s largest government-funded healthcare program” targeting more than 50 crore beneficiaries.
 
• Over 10.74 crore vulnerable entitled families (approximately 50 crore beneficiaries) will be eligible for these benefits.
 
• PMJAY will provide cashless and paperless access to services for the beneficiary at the point of service.
 
• PMJAY will help reduce catastrophic expenditure for hospitalizations, which impoverishes people and will help mitigate the financial risk arising out of catastrophic health episodes.
 
• Entitled families will be able to use the quality health services they need without facing financial hardships.
 
• When fully implemented, PMJAY will become the world’s largest fully government-financed health protection scheme.
 
• It is a visionary step toward advancing the agenda of Universal Health Coverage (UHC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ayushman Bharat is a progression towards promotive, preventive, curative, palliative and rehabilitative aspects of Universal Healthcare through access to Health and Wellness Centers (HWCs).
 
• It adopts a continuum-of-care approach,** comprising two interrelated components**:
 
 
• The creation of 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centres will bring health care closer to the homes of the people.
 
 
 
• These centres will provide **Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC)**, covering both maternal and child health services and non-communicable diseases, including free essential drugs and diagnostic services.

3e

questions.question: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (‘NPCSCB’) – ‘Mission Karmayogi’ was launched with the objective of enhancing governance through Civil Service Capacity Building. Which of the following is NOT one of the six pillars of this programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Physical fitness framework**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Civil Service Capacity Building Program (NPCSCB)** is known as **Mission Karmayogi**.
 
• The Indian bureaucracy has undergone a transformation. On **September 2, 2020**, the Union Cabinet officially unveiled it.
 
• The mission's goal is to provide the groundwork for the capacity building of Indian public employees and to improve governance in the country.
 
• The Union Cabinet has started Mission Karmayogi. Between 2020 and 2025, it intends to construct a new national architecture for civil service capacity building at the person, institutional, and process levels.
 
• To carry out this aim, the Companies Act 2013 establishes a special purpose vehicle (SPV) (a non-profit corporation).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB)** aspires to produce a professional, well-trained, and forward-looking civil service that is imbued with a shared awareness of India's developmental goals, national programmes, and objectives.
 
• The NPCSCB's main goal is to improve the citizen-government interaction and make it easier to live and do business. This requires civil servants to develop both functional and behavioural competencies.
 
• The time from 2014 to 2019 was used to achieve the development pre-requisites, and the next five years will be used to meet the aspirations. **Mission Karmayogi **is part of a longer-term reform movement in public HRM and governance that began in 2015.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about ‘Swachh Survekshan - Urban’ is INCORRECT?

__
 
• Swachh Survekshan - Urban is conducted by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**.
 
• It was** introduced by MoHUA in 2016** as a competitive framework to encourage cities to improve the **status of urban sanitation while encouraging large-scale citizen participation**.
 
• It is the world's** largest urban sanitation and cleanliness survey**.

•

questions.question: The National Jute Policy was formulated in ______, with the objective of increasing productivity, improving quality, ensuring good prices to the jute farmers and enhancing the yield per hectare.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2005__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• National Jute Policy was formulated in 2005 for increasing productivity, improve quality ensure good prices for the jute farmers and enhance the yield per hectare.
 
• The policy objective is to enable the jute industry to build **world-class state-of-the-art manufacturing capabilities**.
 
• Its goal is to encourage **Foreign Direct Investment, research and development** in the sector.
 
• The policy is undertaken by the **Ministry of Textiles**.
 
• Its vision is for **sustainable employment generation and the economic growth of the nation**.
 
• It focuses on **increasing exports to Rs.5000 crore by 2010 from the present level of Rs.1000 crore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **__About Jute__**

 
• It is known as **golden fibre** because it is the most used natural fibre.
 
• Used in making **gunny bags, mats, ropes, yarn, carpets and other artefacts**.
 
• It is cultivated mainly in **eastern India** because of the **rich alluvial soil** of the **Ganga-Brahmaputra delta**.
 
• **India, Bangladesh, China and Thailand** are the world's largest producing countries of Jutes.
 
• For its cultivation is the required temperature between **25-35°C and rainfall of about 150-250 cm**.
 
• The top Jute Producing State is **West Bengal followed by Bihar and Assam**.

questions.question: The ______ aims to provide tap water connection to every rural home by 2024.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Jal Jeevan Mission.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission** is envisioned to provide safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections by **2024 **to all households in rural India.
 
• The programme will also implement source sustainability measures as mandatory elements, such as recharge and reuse through grey water management, water conservation, rain water harvesting.
 
• The Jal Jeevan Mission will be based on a community approach to water and will include extensive information, education, and communication as a key component of the mission. 
 
• It is a flagship programme of the Government of India, launched by Hon'ble Prime Minister on **15th August 2019**.
 
• It will be implemented over 5__ years, with an outlay of Rs 2,87,000 crore.
 
• The government has set aside 50,000 crore rupees for drinking water and ten thousand crore rupees for sanitation.
 
• The budget allocation for Jal Jeevan Mission increased by 450% for 2021.

questions.question: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 aims to provide ____ days of wage employment to every household to ensure livelihood security in rural areas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__100.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA) aims to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.**
 
• Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA) is **an Indian labour law and social security measure that aims to guarantee the right to work.**
 
• The act was passed on** August 23, 2005. (under the prime ministership of Manmohan Singh).**
 
• The act was** first proposed in 1991 by PV.Narasimha Rao.**
 
• It was quoted as a **"Stellar Example of Rural Development" in World Development Report 2014.**
 
• The NDA Government had decided to provide 150 days in rain-hit areas.
 
• Employment is provided within 5 km of an applicant's residence.
 
• If work is not provided within 15 days of applying, applicants are entitled to an unemployment allowance.
 
• The registration process involves an application to the Gram Panchayat and the issue of Job cards.
 
• **MNREGA is implemented mainly by Gram Panchayats.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The act aims to follow** Directive Principles of State Policy enunciated in Part 4** of the Constitution of India.
 
• **Article 41** directs the state to secure all the citizens'** right to Work.**
 
• The act also fulfills** Article 21 **of the Constitution of India which guarantees the** Right to Life with dignity to every citizen of India.**

questions.question: Under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), what is the target year to provide Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) to every rural household in India?

questions.question: In which year was the Immunization Programme introduced in India as 'Expanded Programme of Immunization' (EPI) by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1978.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Immunization Programme introduced in India as the 'Expanded Programme of Immunization' (EPI) by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare was introduced in India in the year **1978**.
 
• It was renamed as **Universal Immunization Programme** in **1985** when its reach was expanded beyond urban areas.
 
• The **objective** of the programme was:
 
 
• To reduce morbidity and mortality from diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, poliomyelitis and childhood tuberculosis by providing immunization services to all eligible children and pregnant women by 1990.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)** is one of the largest public health programmes targeting close to 2.67 crore newborns and 2.9 crore pregnant women annually.
 
• It is one of the most cost-effective public health interventions and is largely responsible for the reduction of vaccine-preventable under-5 mortality rate.
 
• Under UIP, immunization is provided free of cost against **12 vaccine-preventable diseases**.
 
• Nationally against 9 diseases - **Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Polio, Measles, Rubella, a severe form of Childhood Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B and Meningitis & Pneumonia** caused by Hemophilus Influenza type B.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) of the Government of India is available to people in the age group of ______ having a bank account who give their consent to join/enable auto-debit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18 to 50 years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)**__** **

 
 
• The government of India launched Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) **on 09 May 2015.**
 
• It was proposed by the **Finance(Arun Jaitley) Minister in the 2015 budget speech.**
 
• It comes under** the Ministry of Finance.**
 
• It was a** government-backed life insurance scheme in India**
 
• **Aim** - PMJJBY was launched to increase the reach of life insurance among citizens.
 
 
 
• **Other details of PMJJBY;**

 
 

 
 
Primary KYC

 
 
 
Aadhaar will be the primary KYC

 
 
 

 
 
Entry age

 
 
 
**Min – 18 yrs (on the date of enrollment),**

 
**Max- 50 yrs(Age near Birthday)**

 
 
 

 
 
Maximum maturity age

 
 
 
Completion of 55 years (Age near Birthday)

 
 
 

 
 
Coverage terms

 
 
 
1 year (renewable) – **June 1 to May 31 each year**

 
 
 

 
 
Sum assured

 
 
 
Maximum coverage of** Rs. 2,00,000 per life** irrespective of multiple accounts/multiple certificates of insurance held under the PMJJBY scheme.

 
The cover of Rs 2 lakh comes at less than one rupee per day.

 
 
 

 
 
Premium

questions.question: India banned unregulated deposit schemes through an Act passed in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2019.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• India banned unregulated deposit schemes through an Act passed in the year** 2019. **

 
• Unregulated Deposit Schemes were banned in India by the 'Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019'.
 
• Parliament has passed the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Bill, 2019, which seeks to put in place a mechanism by which poor depositors will get back their hard-earned money.
 
• The Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Bill, 2019 was introduced in Lok Sabha by the Minister of Finance, Ms. Nirmala Sitharaman, on July 19, 2019.
 
• It also seeks to amend three laws, i.e., the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, and the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002.
 
• The Bill bans unregulated deposit schemes. A deposit-taking scheme is defined as unregulated if it is taken for a business purpose and is not registered with the regulators.
